meta.description: Assign cells to their sample of origin from cell or nucleus hashing (CITE-seq HTOs, MULTI-seq lipid/cholesterol tags, CellPlex CMOs) and call cross-sample doublets using Seurat HTODemux/MULTIseqDemux, hashsolo, demuxEM, GMM-Demux, and demuxmix. Use when assigning pooled hashed cells back to their sample, calling cross-sample doublets from HTO counts, choosing a demultiplexing method, deciding between hashtag and genetic demultiplexing, or rescuing an oversized Negative pile from weak HTO staining or ambient spillover.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs/PMIDs, p-values, sample sizes, or clinical claims in any of the 5 outputs; all reported numbers trace to executed code or synthetic ground truth.

practice_boundaries.detail: Skill operates on cell/sample data in a lab computational context, not patient diagnosis or treatment; no diagnostic/prescriptive language in any output; a medical disclaimer is not applicable to this scope.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled methodological fallacy found. The cross-sample-doublet / within-sample-doublet distinction, the 1/k calibration heuristic, and the genetic-vs-hashtag applicability rules (Input 4) all matched verified tool behavior and the Skill's own governing principle.

code_usability.detail: All executed code ran to completion without syntax errors, infinite loops, or missing dependencies. Input 2's hashsolo call is a severe accuracy defect (see P0), not an unrunnable-code defect in the strict M4 sense, so it is scored via dynamic_score and recommendations rather than this gate.

functional_suitability.note: Decision table and 2 of 5 named tools (HTODemux, hashsolo) have working examples; demuxEM/pegasus and GMM-Demux have no runnable pattern. hashsolo's own advertised 2-hashtag use case (usage-guide.md) silently fails with default parameters (see Input 2).

reliability.note: No warning anywhere in the Skill about hashsolo's number_of_noise_barcodes default degenerating at 2 tags, or about demuxmix's glm.nb hard-crash on poor fits; neither failure mode surfaces an actionable message to the agent.

performance_context.note: Clean progressive disclosure: SKILL.md ~70 lines, usage-guide.md for prompts/tips, examples/ for code.

agent_usability.note: Governing principle and decision table are clear and consistent; feedback design and error prevention both miss the empirically-found silent-failure mode in Input 2.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language in Quick Start prompts; input-requirement documentation is explicit (Category-3 Forgiveness override applied).

security.note: No credentials, no unsanitized user-string execution, no data-retention concerns; standard local-file bioinformatics workflow.

maintainability.note: Clean file separation (SKILL.md/usage-guide.md/examples/); no bundled expected-output test fixtures to verify future changes against.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger description; excellent Related Skills composability section with correct scope handoffs; all 3 executed tools verified deterministic, but the Skill itself never states this or flags GMM-Demux (untested here) either way.

inputs.label: demuxmix rescue of an oversized Negative pile (weak staining)
inputs.note: Real execution (demuxmix 1.8.0). On realistic overdispersed ambient background, demuxmix outperformed a baseline HTODemux-style quantile call (0.961 vs 0.951 accuracy) as the Skill claims. key_strengths: Governing-principle and decision-table framing (hashtag vs. genetic vs. expression-doublet detection) is accurate and matches verified tool behavior, including the 1/k within-sample-doublet calibration heuristic confirmed on synthetic data (Input 5, 98.8% global accuracy).
HTODemux example (CLR margin=2, positive.quantile=0.99) reproduced ground truth exactly (1600/1600 global, 1360/1360 sample-ID) with zero modification to the Skill's documented pattern.
Tips section covers real, non-obvious pitfalls (minority-tag vs. failed-antibody, nucleus vs. whole-cell capture, CLR margin choice) that a less experienced agent would otherwise miss.
All three tested tools (HTODemux, hashsolo, demuxmix) are verified fully deterministic across repeated runs on identical input -- no unseeded stochastic calls.
Related Skills section correctly scopes handoffs (genetic demux to batch-integration, within-sample doublets to doublet-detection) rather than over-reaching into adjacent skills' territory.

recommendations.title: hashsolo silently misclassifies 100% of cells as Negative with exactly 2 hashtags
recommendations.problem: Following the Skill's own documented pattern (and usage-guide.md's own example prompt 'when I only have two hashtags') with scanpy.external.pp.hashsolo on a 2-tag dataset, every cell is classified Negative regardless of true sample assignment (94.6% error rate vs. ground truth), with no error raised.
recommendations.root_cause: sce.pp.hashsolo's number_of_noise_barcodes parameter defaults to len(cell_hashing_columns) - 2, which is 0 for exactly 2 tags, degenerating the noise-distribution fit; SKILL.md, usage-guide.md, and examples/hashsolo_scanpy.py never mention this parameter.
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit warning in SKILL.md and usage-guide.md: when calling hashsolo with exactly 2 or 3 hashing columns, pass number_of_noise_barcodes explicitly (e.g. 1) instead of relying on the default, and instruct the agent to check that Classification counts are not ~100% Negative before trusting the result.

recommendations.title: No runnable example for demuxEM/pegasus or GMM-Demux
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md and the Version Compatibility line name pegasus/demuxEM and GMM-Demux as recommended tools, but examples/ contains only Seurat HTODemux and scanpy hashsolo patterns.
recommendations.root_cause: Reference examples were written for 2 of the 5 named tools only.
recommendations.fix: Add a short demuxEM/pegasus code pattern (or at minimum a CLI-invocation sketch for GMM-Demux) to examples/, matching the depth of the two existing examples.

recommendations.title: demuxmix's negative-binomial regression can hard-crash rather than degrade gracefully
recommendations.problem: On HTO data with underdispersed ambient background, demuxmix's internal glm.nb fit throws an uncaught R error ('missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed') that halts the R session; demuxmix's own warning correctly names the cause (underdispersion) and suggests clusterInit, but the Skill never mentions this failure mode or remedy.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill's demuxmix guidance ('use demuxmix with the detected-gene count to handle uneven staining') does not cover demuxmix's own documented clusterInit escape hatch for poor GLM fits.
recommendations.fix: Add a tip: if demuxmix throws a glm.nb/underdispersion error or warning, re-run with a manual clusterInit (e.g., k-means on log HTO counts) as demuxmix's own documentation recommends.

recommendations.title: No explicit sanity-check threshold for an oversized Negative pile before trusting output
recommendations.problem: The Tips section warns qualitatively about large Negative piles from weak staining but gives the agent no concrete check to catch a degenerate run (such as Input 2's 100% Negative result) before subsetting or reporting results.
recommendations.root_cause: Guidance is descriptive ('rescue it') rather than a concrete escape-hatch check.
recommendations.fix: Add a line to 'What the Agent Will Do': after classification, if the Negative fraction exceeds roughly 50%, stop and diagnose (wrong tool parameters, failed staining, or barcode mismatch) before proceeding.
